newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE shares edge higher as Ramadan comes to an end.
newsitem.headline: UAE shares edge higher as Ramadan comes to an end.

text.p: Turnover on the informal United Arab Emirates stock market was subdued in the week to Thursday as the country slowed down in the last few days of the Islamic fasting month of Ramadan, dealers said.
Ten shares went up, nudging the National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) 27-share index up 8.9 points to 2,531.86.

Market leader, telecommunications firm Etisalat climbed 25 dirhams, or over two percent, to 1,175 after resuming trade following a week-long break during which a 25 dirham cash dividend was paid to shareholders for the second half of 1996.
The biggest gainer in the week was Abu Dhabi National Insurance, which rose 100 dirhams to 1,200 on expectations that the company might raise its capital this year.
NBAD shares remained at 455. Arab National Bank was up 10 dirhams at 250 and Union National Bank rose five dirhams to 340.
